Imagine on device

Local LLM inference for JavaScript

Run the model on the device. Let the interface imagine.

Boole is a terminal for GGUF models. It runs them on your machine through llama.cpp: no API key, and no per-token cloud bill. Imagine OS is the direction from here. The interface should evolve around how you use the device, with the model staying local.

Today Direction Machine

Today

0.0.1

Version 0.0.1 is a Node.js command line. Four commands work. serve and list are reserved and not implemented yet.

run

Prompt a model. Use an alias such as llama3, a full specifier like TheBloke/Llama-2-7B-GGUF:Q4_K_M, or a local .gguf path. An alias resolves to a Hugging Face repo, then Boole picks the highest-quality quantization that fits in available memory.

pull

Download that file into a local cache. An interrupted download resumes instead of starting over.

doctor

Report the OS, memory, and GPU backend, then suggest a model size this machine can hold.

models

List the aliases shipped with the CLI, including llama3, mistral, phi3, and qwen2.5.

The model’s text is the only thing written to stdout. Progress and errors stay on stderr. GPU support follows node-llama-cpp: Metal on Apple Silicon, CUDA or Vulkan where that runtime provides them, and CPU otherwise. If node-llama-cpp is not installed, Boole says so and exits. A local server, when it exists, should stay on localhost.

Direction

roadmap

Targets, not measured results. Boole has not published a benchmark for these.

Ternary weights

BitNet-style 1.58-bit models, so a full network can live on the device instead of in a datacenter.

20B at 200 tokens per second

A 20-billion-parameter model with a speed target of 200 tokens per second. That figure is a goal. It is not a result we have recorded.

Imagine OS

The interface should change with how you actually use the machine. A fixed native shell is the starting point, not the finished product. The model still runs locally.

This machine

stack

Inference is a process on the computer that asked for it. After the weights are cached, that run does not need a network round trip.

Language
TypeScript on Node.js 18+
Packages
@boole/cli and @boole/hardware
Runtime
llama.cpp through node-llama-cpp
Weights

License

Where it runs

  • macOS, Apple SiliconMetal
  • macOS, IntelCPU
  • Linux, x86_64CUDA, Vulkan, or CPU
  • Windows, x86_64CUDA, Vulkan, or CPU

There is no API key and no per-token invoice for the run itself. Install with npx @boole/cli or npm i -g @boole/cli. The source and the npm package are public.

Terminal

example 
$ boole run llama3 -p "Explain what a boolean is in one sentence."
llama3 -> bartowski/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-GGUF:<quant>
  highest quality quantization that fits available RAM

A boolean holds one of two values — true or false.

Illustrative session, not a timing result. The quantization depends on the memory free on that machine. stdout is only the model’s text.
